study.title: Cerebral cortex functional networks of magnetic stimulation at acupoints along the pericardium meridian
study.study_design: Within-subject EEG study with resting state and two magnetic stimulation conditions
study.population: Healthy right-handed subjects aged 21 to 25 years old without history of mental illness
study.inclusion_criteria: Healthy right-handed subjects aged 21 to 25 years old without history of mental illness

extraction_notes.note: No sham/placebo control condition was included. The study compares resting state to magnetic stimulation at two acupoints (PC6 and PC7) only, with no sham acupuncture or non-acupoint control arm.
Sensory/interoceptive responses (deqi, pain, etc.) during magnetic stimulation were not assessed or reported.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events were not mentioned in the paper.

No individual MNI coordinates for specific network nodes are reported in the text or tables. Nodes are identified by Brodmann Area labels only. Figure 3 shows source localization with MNI coordinates mentioned (e.g., [X,Y,Z]=[20,-50,70][mm]; [2.90E-2]; 1) but these appear to be for a single exemplar component illustration rather than a full coordinate table.

The paper reports percentage changes in number of connections for functional areas (e.g., movement decreased by 7.3% and 19.9%; advanced cognition increased by 24.9% and 18.8%) but does not provide inferential statistics (t-values, F-values, p-values) for these between-condition comparisons of connection counts.

The descriptions of individual Brodmann Area changes in node number and mean degree (Results section) are narrative summaries. No quantitative values (actual counts or mean degree numbers) are given per BA beyond the aggregate Table 1 data.

Figure 6 shows number of nodes and mean degree per Brodmann Area for resting state, PC7, and PC6 conditions, but exact numerical values cannot be reliably extracted from the figure without the underlying data.

The stimulation device is described as Magstim Rapid2 repetitive pulse magnetic stimulator with an '8'-shaped coil (model number 9925-00). This is TMS/rTMS-like magnetic stimulation applied over acupoints on the forearm/wrist, not transcranial magnetic stimulation or traditional needle acupuncture. The acupuncture_modality field is coded as 'other' given that this modality does not map directly to standard acupuncture modalities.

The order of conditions within subjects is fixed (resting state → PC7 stimulation → 60-minute rest → PC6 stimulation), which may introduce order effects. The paper does not address counterbalancing or order effects.

The paper uses alpha-band cross-correlation for network edges but does not specify the exact alpha-band frequency range (typically 8-13 Hz). Only '0.5-40 Hz band-pass filtering' is mentioned for preprocessing.
EEG sampling frequency is 1000 Hz. Stimulation frequency is 1 Hz. No specific information is provided about artifact rejection related to the magnetic stimulation pulses in the EEG signal.
The number of ICA components selected and the criteria for selecting 'components related to brain activity' are not described in detail.
